value: MWCC GC 1.2.5. QUANTITATIVE STRENGTHENING of claim.law.zero-remat-choice-differs-between-identical-sibling-loops.20260831.v1, and a BOUND on clause (B) of claim.law.variable-identity-reopens-address-pre-and-zero-copy.20260831.v1. When a function contains several zero-initialised induction carriers, the number of `li`-plus-copy preheaders is CONSERVED under source-level changes to carrier identity: giving one loop its own symbol does not create a rematerialised zero, it merely MOVES the copy to another loop, and usually to more than one. Five independent probes on fn_8001267C - dead-local reuse, a fresh declaration, dead-window reuse, and two earlier per-loop splits - never once reduced the total, and the three tried in this pass each made it worse by 38 to 44 real. The variable-identity law is right that a carrier split can close a NAMED cluster (probe B closed the texmod cluster completely) and wrong only if that is read as a route to closing the FUNCTION; the allocator relocates the cost rather than paying it. PRACTICAL RULE, which supersedes spending probes on this shape: on the `li` + `mr`/`addi rD,rS,0` preheader signature, count the affected preheaders first. If more than one loop in the function shows it, treat the set as a single conserved allocator decision and cap immediately - the parent sibling-loop law already proves the choice is made downstream of the source, and this law adds that no redistribution of source symbols can reduce the count. Spend probes here ONLY when exactly one preheader is affected and the function has no sibling carrier loop for the allocator to move the copy into. The class remains WebFrank territory: the substitution is an opcode change with a constant-value side condition, so it needs the dataflow-equivalence audit described in claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source.20260831.v1 and cannot reuse copy_register_fields.
